delete.summary: Delete a package by ID, removing it from the repository holding it.
delete.description:
Deleting needs the same permission publishing does, and it is held over the repository rather
            than over the package: anyone who may publish to a repository may delete any package in it,
            including one somebody else published.

A package the caller may not see is a `404`, and so is one that was already deleted, so
            a repeated delete is indistinguishable from a first one.

A failure of the pacman tools is a `500` like any other failed `ICliTool` rather
            than a `409`: nothing was deleted, the package is still listed and still installable,
            and the caller cannot fix it by sending a different request.

post.summary:
Publish a package file into a repository, creating it or replacing the version already
there.
post.description:
The request body is the raw package file, as `application/octet-stream`. There is
            deliberately no `multipart/form-data` envelope: the name the file is stored under is
            derived from the metadata libalpm reads out of it, so a form would carry nothing worth
            trusting, and a raw body is markedly simpler to stream without buffering.

Package files run to hundreds of megabytes, so the request's own body limit is raised from
            Kestrel's 30 MB default to the configured ceiling before the body is touched. Over that, the
            upload is a `413`.

parameters.description: The repository to publish into.

get.summary: Download a package's file by the package's ID.
get.description:
The response carries a `Content-Disposition` naming the file as it is stored —
            `{name}-{version}-{architecture}.pkg.tar.{ext}`, the basename `repo-add` recorded
            — so a client that saves it to disk ends up with the name pacman expects rather than a
            package id. The body is streamed from disk and never buffered, since a package file can run
            to hundreds of megabytes.

This downloads one package by identity. It is not a pacman mirror: a client configured with
            `Server = …` needs the repository's `.db.tar.gz` and every package file resolvable
            under one base URL by basename, which is separate work.
